paragraphs.source_en: one's own superiority is merely a phenomenon that appears as the inevitable result after carrying out such means. Therefore, when one wishes on the one hand to display one's own superiority, yet does not care to do real harm to others, teasing them is the most suitable thing imaginable. Unless one inflicts some slight injury on another, one's greatness cannot be proved as a matter of fact. If it does not emerge as an actual fact, then however secure one may feel in one's head, the pleasure is surprisingly diminished. Human beings are creatures who rely on themselves. Even when self-reliance is hard to come by, they still want to cling to it. For that very reason, unless they try applying their strength to others in practice, to prove that they are dependable and may safely be trusted, they cannot be satisfied. Moreover, the more they are vulgar fools who understand no reasoning, and the more uneasy they are because they cannot much rely on themselves, the more they try to seize every opportunity to obtain this certificate. It is the same as a practitioner of jujutsu wanting now and then to throw someone. Those whose jujutsu is dubious walk about the neighborhood because they cherish the extremely dangerous notion that somehow, just once, they would like to encounter someone weaker than themselves. Even an amateur would do, so long as they could give him a good throw. There are various other reasons besides, but the discussion would grow too long, so permit me to omit them. If you want to hear them, bring me a box of dried bonito and come to learn. I shall teach you at any time. If, taking what I have said above as reference, we reason from it, then in my opinion mountain monkeys and schoolteachers are the most convenient objects to tease. Here it may seem rather improper to compare schoolteachers with mountain monkeys; not improper toward the monkeys, but rather improper toward the teachers. Yet they resemble each other so closely that it cannot be helped. As you know, monkeys brought from the mountains are chained up; however much they bare their teeth and screech, there is no fear of being scratched by them. Teachers are not chained, but instead they are bound hand and foot by their salaries, so however much you tease them it is safe; they will not resign and go slap their students. If they had the courage to resign, they would never have become teachers in the first place and taken up the work of babysitting students. My master is a teacher. He is not a teacher at Rakun Hall, but he is unquestionably a teacher all the same. He is eminently suitable for teasing, eminently easy, and an eminently harmless man. The students of Rakun Hall are boys; they understand that teasing others is what raises their own noses in pride, and they even regard it as a right that, as the fruit of education, may properly be demanded. Not only that, if they did not tease someone, how ought they to employ their energetic limbs and brains? During the ten-minute recess, they are a company of people at a loss from sheer idleness. When these conditions are present, the students naturally do the teasing and my master naturally gets teased. No matter who is asked, there is not the least unreasonableness in it.

units.source_en: Here it may seem rather improper to compare schoolteachers with mountain monkeys; not improper toward the monkeys, but rather improper toward the teachers.
units.source_zh: 在这里，我将学校的教师和深山老林的猴子相提并论，似乎有些不太恭敬——不是对猴子不恭敬，而是对教师不大恭敬。

units.source_en: Yet they resemble each other so closely that it cannot be helped.
units.source_zh: 然而他们太相似了，又有什么办法呢。

units.source_zh: 如尊驾所知，从深山抓来的猴子都是用锁链锁起来的，不管它们怎样龇牙咆哮，它也挠不着人。

units.source_en: Teachers are not chained, but instead they are bound hand and foot by their salaries, so however much you tease them it is safe; they will not resign and go slap their students.

ja.t: られている。いくらからかったって

units.source_zh: 教师虽未被锁链锁起来，但却被薪俸捆住了手脚，所以你怎样捉弄他也不碍事，他不会辞职去打学生的耳光。

ja.t: のあるようなものなら

units.source_zh: 如果他有辞职的勇气，那么他最初就不会当教师干那种哄学生的职业了。

units.source_en: My master is a teacher. He is not a teacher at Rakun Hall, but he is unquestionably a teacher all the same.
units.source_zh: 我家主人是教师，他虽不是落云馆的教师，但毕竟还是教师无疑。

units.source_en: He is eminently suitable for teasing, eminently easy, and an eminently harmless man.
units.source_zh: 捉弄他是最最合适的，是不费吹灰之力的，而且他又是个最老实的家伙。

units.source_en: The students of Rakun Hall are boys; they understand that teasing others is what raises their own noses in pride, and they even regard it as a right that, as the fruit of education, may properly be demanded.
units.source_zh: 落云馆的学生都是少年，他们都很明白，捉弄人可以显示出他们了不起，作为教育的成果，他们具有当然的权利实行这样正当的要求。

units.source_en: Not only that, if they did not tease someone, how ought they to employ their energetic limbs and brains?

ja.t: のみならずからかいでもしなければ、

units.source_zh: 不仅如此，如果不捉弄人，他们那充满活力的四肢和头脑，应当如何去使用呢？

units.source_en: During the ten-minute recess, they are a company of people at a loss from sheer idleness.
units.source_zh: 在十分钟的课间休息时，他们都是一群闲得发慌的人啊。

units.source_en: When these conditions are present, the students naturally do the teasing and my master naturally gets teased.
units.source_zh: 由于具备这些条件，所以学生们自然要去捉弄人，而主人自然要被捉弄。

units.source_en: No matter who is asked, there is not the least unreasonableness in it.
units.source_zh: 这不论让谁来说，都是十分合乎道理的。

paragraphs.source_zh: 自己的优势，只不过是在实施这些手段之后产生的必然结果而出现的现象。因此，一方面希望显示自己的优势，但又不愿意加害于人，在这种情况下，捉弄人是最好不过的了。如果不给人以少许伤害，则不足以从事实上证明自己的了不起。如果不表现为事实，那么尽管在内心里感到不冒风险，快乐也要减去大半。人总是自信的。即使是难以自信的时候，也还是要抱着自信不放。正因为如此，人总想对他人实际运用一下自己的力量，以证明自己是可信的，可以放心的。而且，越是那些不明事理的蠢材，对自己终日惶惶不安的人，越是想利用一切机会获得这份证明。这和会柔道的人总想将他人摔出去是一样的。那些在柔术上二流的人之所以总在街道上转悠，就是因为他有一种危险的想法，希望哪怕一次也好，能碰上一个不如自己的人。即使是外行人也没关系，以便狠狠地摔他一跤。除此之外，还有其他种种原因，说下去话就长啦，所以请允许我从略。如果你还想听，那就请你带盒干松鱼来找我。我随时都会告诉你的。如果将以上所说作为参考加以推论的话，按我的想法，深山老林中的猴子和学校中的教师是最适合于被捉弄对象的。在这里，我将学校的教师和深山老林的猴子相提并论，似乎有些不太恭敬——不是对猴子不恭敬，而是对教师不大恭敬。然而他们太相似了，又有什么办法呢。如尊驾所知，从深山抓来的猴子都是用锁链锁起来的，不管它们怎样龇牙咆哮，它也挠不着人。教师虽未被锁链锁起来，但却被薪俸捆住了手脚，所以你怎样捉弄他也不碍事，他不会辞职去打学生的耳光。如果他有辞职的勇气，那么他最初就不会当教师干那种哄学生的职业了。我家主人是教师，他虽不是落云馆的教师，但毕竟还是教师无疑。捉弄他是最最合适的，是不费吹灰之力的，而且他又是个最老实的家伙。落云馆的学生都是少年，他们都很明白，捉弄人可以显示出他们了不起，作为教育的成果，他们具有当然的权利实行这样正当的要求。不仅如此，如果不捉弄人，他们那充满活力的四肢和头脑，应当如何去使用呢？在十分钟的课间休息时，他们都是一群闲得发慌的人啊。由于具备这些条件，所以学生们自然要去捉弄人，而主人自然要被捉弄。这不论让谁来说，都是十分合乎道理的。

paragraphs.source_en: For my master to grow angry at this is the height of boorishness, the very summit of stupidity. I shall now set down, one by one, how the students of Rakun Hall teased my master, and how boorishly my master responded, for your inspection.

units.source_en: For my master to grow angry at this is the height of boorishness, the very summit of stupidity.
units.source_zh: 主人为此而发怒，真是极不识趣，是愚蠢透顶的。

units.source_en: I shall now set down, one by one, how the students of Rakun Hall teased my master, and how boorishly my master responded, for your inspection.

ja.t: にからかったか、これに

units.source_zh: 下边我就将落云馆的学生是如何捉弄主人，而主人对此又是如何的不识趣一一写下来，向您介绍一番吧。

paragraphs.source_zh: 主人为此而发怒，真是极不识趣，是愚蠢透顶的。下边我就将落云馆的学生是如何捉弄主人，而主人对此又是如何的不识趣一一写下来，向您介绍一番吧。
